{{Short description|American mathematician (1923–2016)}}
'''Willem V. R. Malkus''' (November 19, 1923 – May 28, 2016) was an American researcher of [[applied mathematics]]. A professor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] from 1969 to 1996, he was one of the inventors of the [[Malkus waterwheel]].<ref name=":0" />

Malkus was a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Geophysical Union]], and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. He received two [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]s. He is a son of [[Alida Malkus]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2016-06-08 |title=Willem Malkus, professor emeritus of mathematics, dies at 92 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2016/willem-malkus-professor-emeritus-mathematics-dies-0608 |access-date=2026-06-18 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref>
